channel.title: HB
channel.description: HB is a loosely bound tech law publication about governance, procedure, institutional design, and the legal edges of technical systems.

item.title: When Model Opacity Becomes a Due Process Problem
item.description: A HB article on how automated opacity turns from technical complexity into a due process and accountability problem.

item.title: Scraping, Consent, and the New Public Access Fights
item.description: A HB essay on scraping disputes, contractual fences, and the shrinking practical meaning of public online space.

item.title: Law School AI Policies Are Becoming Shadow Curricula
item.description: A HB article on how classroom AI policies quietly teach authorship, delegation, and professional responsibility.

item.title: Content Moderation Needs an Audit Trail, Not a Press Release
item.description: A HB essay arguing that platform legitimacy depends on durable audit trails, records, and reviewable moderation procedures.
